title: The lineage of Ikshvaku
introduction: Ikshvaku's bloodline is narrated as custom demands to enquire into the bridegroom's lineage. Vashishta narrates this to other Kushadhvaja, who is also summoned to participate in the wedding celebrations, and who later has to offer his two daughters to Bharata and Shatrughna. This listing and eulogising ancestors is an adjunctive custom in Indian marriages. Nowadays it is limited to cite only three preceding generations, instead of narrating from the first, since nobody holds his family tree, ready at hand.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे सप्ततितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 70th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रभाते जनकः कृतकर्मा महर्षिभिः |
उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञः शतानंदं पुरोहितम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ prabhāte janakaḥ kṛta karmā maharṣibhiḥ |
uvāca vākyam vākyajñaḥ śatānandam purohitam
verses.translation: Then on the next day morning after getting the ritual liturgies performed through sages, he that articulator Janaka articulated this to sage Shataananda, the royal priest.

verses.devanagari:
भ्राता मम महातेजा यवीयानतिधार्मिकः |
कुशध्वज इति ख्यातः पुरीमध्यवसच्छुभाम्
वार्या फलकपर्यन्तां पिबन्निक्षुमतीं नदीम् |
सांकाश्यां पुण्यसंकाशां विमानमिव पुष्पकम्
verses.iast:
bhrātā mama mahātejā yavīyān atidhārmikaḥ |
kuśadhvaja iti khyātaḥ purīm adhyavasat śubhām
vāryā phalaka paryantām piban ikṣumatīm nadīm |
sāṅkāśyām puṇya saṅkāśām vimānam iva puṣpakam
verses.translation: "My younger brother renowned thus as Kushadhvaja, a highly self-righteous one and a highly brilliant one is ruling from the auspicious and holy city named Saankaasya, which city is surrounded by River Ikshumati as a natural moat, in which moat bastions of tridents are staked all around... and my brother presides over that city as if he is sitting in the Pushpaka aircraft of richly-rich god Kubera, and as though supping the sugarcane juice-like waters of River Ikshumati...
notes: The words vāryā phalaka paryantām also mean 'that city is surrounded by the plantation of citrus grapefruits that are famous for health keeping.

glosses.meaning: River Ikshumati [with sugar-cane juice like waters]
in water [of moats,] staked trident [bastions,] all around
holiness, equal to - a holy city

verses.devanagari:
तमहं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि यज्ञगोप्ता स मे मतः |
प्रीतिं सोऽपि महातेजा इमां भोक्ता मया सह
verses.iast:
tam aham draṣṭum icchāmi yajña goptā sa me mataḥ |
prītim so api mahātejā imām bhoktā mayā saha
verses.translation: "And I wish to see him, as he is the nominated benefactor of this Vedic-ritual of mine, and he too shall become a rejoicer in partaking the joyousness of this marriage... " So said Janaka to Shataananda.
notes: Kushadhvaja supplied whole lot of paraphernalia for this Vedic-ritual of Janaka from his auspicious city Saankaasya, and hence he is the benefactor of the ritual.

glosses.meaning: I, him, to see, I wish
= he, my, Vedic-ritual's, protector- benefactor, agreed to be - he is nominated as supplier of all paraphernalia to the ritual
me, along with, this [marriage,] joyousness of, will be rejoicer.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्ते तु वचने शतानंदस्य संनिधौ |
आगताः केचिदव्यग्रा जनकस्तान् समादिशत्
verses.iast:
evam ukto tu vacane śatānandasya saṃnidhau |
āgatāḥ kecid avyagrā janakaḥ tān samādiśat
verses.translation: That way when Janaka asseverated that enunciation in the presence of Shataananda, Shataananda in turn ordered and summoned envoys, and then some alacritous envoys have come, whom Janaka ordered to proceed to his brother.

glosses.meaning: that way, words [enunciation,] after saying [on asseverating,] while being so

verses.devanagari:
शासनात्तु नरेन्द्रस्य प्रययुः शीघ्रवाजिभिः |
समानेतुं नरव्याघ्रं विष्णुमिन्द्राज्ञया यथा
verses.iast:
śāsanāt tu narendrasya prayayuḥ śīghra vājibhiḥ |
samānetum naravyāghram viṣṇum indra ājñayā yathā
verses.translation: By the order of the king those envoys who have speedy horses have travelled on to city Saankaasya speedily, to lead forth that manly-tiger Kushadhvaja that speedily, which is as good as fetching Vishnu by order of Indra.

glosses.meaning: Indra, by order of, Vishnu, as with - to fetch Vishnu as per Indra's order
[those envoys that] have speedy, horses, travelled.

verses.devanagari:
सांकाश्यां ते समागम्य ददृशुश्च कुशध्वजम् |
न्यवेदयन् यथावृत्तं जनकस्य च चिन्तितम्
verses.iast:
saṅkāsyām te samāgaṃya dadṛśuḥ ca kuśdhvajam |
nyavedayan yathā vṛttam janakasya ca cintitam
verses.translation: On arriving in city Saankaasya those envoys have seen king Kushadhvaja and on submitting what has happened to the king about Rama's breaking of Shiva's bow, and they have also submitted the point of view of Janaka regarding marriages of four daughters.
notes: The viewpoint of Janaka is to offset the problem of marriages of both the daughters of his brother Kushadhvaja. Dasharatha has four sons and Janaka presaged a quadruple alliance with him, where Janaka has two daughters and his brother Kushadhvaja has two.

glosses.meaning: Janaka's, thought of [point of view,] even

verses.devanagari:
तद्वृत्तं नृपतिः श्रुत्वा दूतश्रेष्ठैर्महाजवैः |
आज्ञया तु नरेन्द्रस्य आजगाम कुशध्वजः
verses.iast:
tad vṛttam nṛpatiḥ śrutvā dūta śreṣṭhaiḥ mahā javaiḥ |
ājñayā tu narendrasya ājagāma kuśadhvajaḥ
verses.translation: On hearing that event from the worthy envoys whose speed is praiseworthy, king Kushadhvaja came right away to Mithila by the order of king Janaka.

glosses.meaning: by king Janaka's, order, came forth [to Mithila.]

verses.devanagari:
स ददर्श महात्मानं जनकं धर्मवत्सलम् |
सोऽभिवाद्य शतानंदं जनकं चातिधार्मिकम्
राजार्हं परमं दिव्यमासनं चाध्यरोहत |
verses.iast:
sa dadarśa mahātmānam janakam dharma vatsalam |
so abhivādya śatānandam janakam ca ati dhārmikam
rāja arham paramam divyam āsanam ca adhyarohata |
verses.translation: Kushadhvaja addressed himself to the insightful one and a compassionate person in the duty of an elder brother, namely Janaka, and on reverencing sage Shataananda firstly, next he has reverenced his fondly affectionate brother Janaka, and then he sat upon a majestic seat, that which is befitting to kings.

glosses.meaning: towards duty [of an elder brother,] a compassionate one - one who is helping as an elder brother

verses.devanagari:
उपविष्टावुभौ तौ तु भ्रातरावमितौजसौ
प्रेषयामासतुर्वीरौ मन्त्रिश्रेष्ठं सुदामनम् |
verses.iast:
upaviṣṭau ubhau tau tu bhrātarau amita ojasau
preṣayāmāsatuḥ vīrau mantri śreṣṭham sudāmanam |
verses.translation: Both the brothers of unlimited self-refulgence having assumed their high seats, they who are distinguished for their righteous acts have started to send Sudaamana, the distinguished minister.

glosses.meaning: those two, valorous [distinguished brothers for their righteous acts]

verses.devanagari:
गच्छ मंत्रिपते शीघ्रमैक्ष्वाकममितप्रभम्
आत्मजैः सह दुर्धर्षमानयस्व समंत्रिणम् |
verses.iast:
gaccha mantri pate śīghram ikṣvākam amita prabham
ātmajaiḥ saha durdharṣam ānayasva sa mantriṇam |
verses.translation: "Oh, minister plenipotentiary, Sudaamana, you please proceed immediately to king Dasharatha, the legatee of Ikshvaku-s with illimitable resplendence, and let that invincible king Dasharatha be led hither along with his sons and along with his Vedic-celebrants..." Thus Janaka ordered Sudaamana, the minister.

glosses.meaning: to one with - un, limited, resplendence
who will be - with, ministers [Vedic celebrants]

verses.devanagari:
औपकार्यां स गत्वा तु रघूणां कुलवर्धनम्
ददर्श शिरसा चैनमभिवाद्येदमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
aupakāryām sa gatvā tu raghūṇām kula vardhanam
dadarśa śirasā ca enam abhivādya idam abravīt |
verses.translation: Accordingly Sudaamana has gone to the visitatorial-palace of the promoter of Raghu's heritage, namely Dasharatha, and he said this on appearing before that king duly bowing down and hailing the king.

glosses.meaning: of Raghu's, heritage, promoter of - Dasharatha
him, with head [head-bent, bow down] on hailing, also

verses.devanagari:
अयोध्याधिपते वीर वैदेहो मिथिलाधिपः
स त्वां द्रष्टुं व्यवसितः सोपाध्यायपुरोहितम् |
verses.iast:
ayodhyā adhipate vīra vaideho mithilā adhipaḥ
sa tvām draṣṭum vyavasitaḥ sa upādhyāya purohitam |
verses.translation: "Oh, valiant king, oh, sovereign of Ayodhya, his highness the sovereign of Mithila from the heritage of Videha kings is poised for seeking an audience with your highness, along with your highness' royal-priest Vashishta and other mentors..." The minister Sudaamana said so to Dasharatha.

glosses.meaning: he, the king of Videha heritage - Janaka
you, to see [seeking an audience,] poised for.

verses.devanagari:
मंत्रिश्रेष्ठवचः श्रुत्वा राजा सर्षिगणस्तदा
सबन्धुरगमत्तत्र जनको यत्र वर्तते |
verses.iast:
mantri śreṣṭha vacaḥ śrutvā rājā sa ṛṣi gaṇaḥ tadā
sa bandhuḥ agamat tatra janako yatra var.htate |
verses.translation: On hearing that best minister's words, then king Dasharatha came to the place where Janaka is available, along with his kinsmen and the assemblages of sages.

glosses.meaning: minister, best one's, words, on hearing

verses.devanagari:
राजा च मंत्रिसहितः सोपाध्यायः सबांधवः
वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठो वैदेहमिदमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
rājā ca mantri sahitaḥ sa upādhyāyaḥ sa bāndhavaḥ
vākyam vākya vidām śreṣṭho vaideham idam abravīt |
verses.translation: That sententious king Dasharatha said this to the king from the lineage of Videha kings, Janaka, who is with his mentors, kinsfolk, and ministers.

glosses.meaning: sentence, experts in making, the best [sententious king Dasharatha]
to king from the linage of Videha, this, sentence, said.

verses.devanagari:
विदितं ते महाराज इक्ष्वाकुकुलदैवतम्
वक्ता सर्वेषु कृत्येषु वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः |
verses.iast:
viditam te mahārāja ikṣvāku kula daivatam
vaktā sarveṣu kṛtyeṣu vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ |
verses.translation: "Oh, exalted king Janaka, you already appreciate that this godly sage Vashishta is godlike to the bloodline of Ikshvaku-s, and in all affairs he is our internuncio...

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्राभ्यनुज्ञातः सह सर्वैर्महर्षिभिः
एष वक्ष्यति धर्मात्मा वसिष्ठो मे यथाक्रमम् |
तूष्णींभूते दशरथे वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः
उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो वैदेहं सपुरोधसाम् |
verses.iast:
viśvāmitra abhyanujñātaḥ saha sarvaiḥ mahar.hṣibhiḥ
eṣa vakṣyati dharmātmā vasiṣṭho me yathā kramam |
tūṣṇīm bhūte daśarathe vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
uvāca vākyam vākyajño vaideham sa purodhasām |
verses.translation: "Should an assent be given by Sage Vishvamitra, along with all the great sages present here, this equanimous Vashishta will narrate about my bloodline, lineally..." And, to the nod of Vishvamitra Dasharatha become reticent, and then the godly and sententious sage Vashishta who is along with his men of the cloth said these sentences to the king of Videha, namely Janaka.

glosses.meaning: silent, on becoming - when took pause

verses.devanagari:
अव्यक्तप्रभवो ब्रह्मा शाश्वतो नित्य अव्ययः
तस्मान्मरीचिः संजज्ञे मरीचेः कश्यपः सुतः |
विवस्वान् कश्यपाज्जज्ञे मनुर्वैवस्वतः स्मृतः
verses.iast:
avyakta prabhavo brahmā śāśvato nitya avyayaḥ
tasmāt marīciḥ sañjajñe marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ |
vivasvān kaśyapāt jajñe manur vaivasvataḥ smṛtaḥ
verses.translation: "The Unprovable emanated the timeless, changeless and perishless Brahma, and from that Being, namely Brahma, Mariichi is begotten, and Kaashyapa is the son of Mariichi, and the Sun is begotten from Kaashyapa, and Manu is said to be the son of the Sun...
notes: The avyakta is the 'Unmanifest' of advaita tenet. Here it an 'Unprovable' entity since it cannot be proved by pramāṇa-s 'source of knowledge' like pratyakśa, anumana, tarka, āgama... 'perception, inference, logic, scriptures...' and because Vishnu cannot be deduced by these sources of knowledge, Vishnu Himself becomes the avyakta. And from the viewpoint of mythology, Ramayana has no place for a 'featureless Absolute...' nir guṇa brahma of advaita, because Valmiki's initial questions to Narada include ko guṇavān, and thus He is sa guṇa brahma. Hence avykta or ākāśa, a kāśa, 'minus, leeway...' all-pervading...' is Vishnu, the 'Unprovable'.

This ākāśa is the often repeated expression in Upanishad-s, telling it to be the ātma, Absolute, abiding in each individual jīva ātma, Individual Soul. ākāśo ha vai nāma rūpayoḥ nirvahitāḥ te yad antara tad brahma tad amṛtam sa ātmā - cāndogya - 8-14 | ko he vāṇyatkaḥ prāṇāt ya eṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt - taittarīya - 7 anuvāka | ākāśor arthāntaratvādivyapadeśāt - 1-3-41 | dahara uttarebhyaḥ - 1-3-14 - brahma sūtra ;'who is he to be able to balance himself if this ākāśa is not to be there...' Taittarriya; 'that which makes the names and forms is within you alone as your innermost inner-space, that alone is deathless...' Chanandogya; 'akaasha [is Absolute] because it is proclaimed to be something different etc., [from names and forms yet their revealer...]; 'the small [aakaasha] is Absolute because of subsequent texts [which give ample evidence of it...] Brahma Sutra. Hence, it is Vishnu.

Out of the three epithets to Brahma one is 'timeless' because He continues to be in two para artha-s, say 31, 10, 40, 00, 00, 00, 000 human years, without transmutation, yet He continues further. He is 'changeless' as his faculties or His divine being does not undergo any mutation or metamorphosis. He is 'perishless' during the above period and after, since Vishnu gave rise to Him. Up to here is ultramundane order of progeny and the mundane lineage is now continued.

glosses.meaning: from, that [Being, Brahma,] Mariichi, is begotten
of Mariici, Kaashyapa, is the son
= Manu, is said to be the son.

verses.devanagari:
मनुः प्रजापतिः पूर्वमिक्ष्वाकुश्च मनोः सुतः |
तमिक्ष्वाकुमयोध्यायां राजानं विद्धि पूर्वकम्
verses.iast:
manuḥ prajāpatiḥ pūrvam ikṣvākuḥ ca manoḥ sutaḥ |
tam ikṣvākum ayodhyāyām rājānam viddhi pūrvakam
verses.translation: "Manu is the earliest Prajaapati and Ikshvaaku is the son of Manu, and that Ikshvaaku is the first king of Ayodhya... know thus...

verses.devanagari:
इक्ष्वाकोस्तु सुतः श्रीमान् कुक्षिरित्येव विश्रुतः |
कुक्षेरथात्मजः श्रीमान् विकुक्षिरुपपद्यत
verses.iast:
ikṣvākoḥ tu sutaḥ śrīmān kukṣiḥ iti eva viśrutaḥ |
kukṣeḥ atha ātmajaḥ śrīmān vikukśiḥ upapadyata
verses.translation: "The son of Ikshvaaku is the legendary Kukshi, thus he is renowned, and the famous Vikukshi is the son of Kukshi...

glosses.meaning: legendary one, Kukshi, thus, only, renowned

verses.devanagari:
विकुक्षेस्तु महातेजा बाणः पुत्रः प्रतापवान् |
बाणस्य तु महातेजा अनरण्यः प्रतापवान्
verses.iast:
vikukśeḥ tu mahātejā bāṇaḥ putraḥ pratāpavān |
bāṇasya tu mahātejā anaraṇyaḥ pratāpavān
verses.translation: "From that most brilliant and courageous Vikukshi, Baana emerged as son, and the highly refulgent and valinat Anaranya is the son of Baana...

verses.devanagari:
अनरण्यात्पृथुर्जज्ञे त्रिशंकुस्तु पृथोः सुतः |
त्रिशंकोरभवत्पुत्रो धुन्धुमारो महायशाः
verses.iast:
anaraṇyāt pṛthuḥ jajñe triśaṅkuḥ tu pṛthoḥ sutaḥ |
triśaṅkoḥ abhavat putro dhundhumāraḥ mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: "Pruthu is the son of Anaranya, and Trishanku is Pruthu's son, and the highly renowned Dhundumaara happened to be the son of Trishanku...

glosses.meaning: highly renowned one, Dhundumaara, son, emerged as.

verses.devanagari:
धुन्धुमारान्महातेजा युवनाश्वो महारथः |
युवनाश्वसुतस्त्वासीन्मान्धाता पृथिवीपतिः
verses.iast:
dhundhumārāt mahātejā yuvanāśvo mahārathaḥ |
yuvanāśva sutaḥ asīt māndhātā pṛthivī patiḥ
verses.translation: "Dhundumaara begot a highly glorious and a speediest charioteer Yuvanaashva as son, and Mandhaata emerged as the son of Yuvanaashva...

glosses.meaning: highly glorious one, speediest charioteer, Yuvanaashva - is the son

verses.devanagari:
मान्धातुस्तु सुतः श्रीमान् सुसन्धिरुदपद्यत |
सुसंधेरपि पुत्रौ द्वौ ध्रुवसंधिः प्रसेनजित्
verses.iast:
māndhātuḥ tu sutaḥ śrīmān susandhiḥ udapadyata |
susandheḥ api putrau dvau dhruvasandhiḥ prasenajit
verses.translation: "Maandhaata engendered the highly noble Susandhi as son, and even Susandhi engendered two sons, namely Dhruvasandhi and Prasenajit...

verses.devanagari:
यशस्वी ध्रुवसंधेस्तु भरतो नाम नामतः |
भरतात्तु महातेजा असितो नाम जायत
verses.iast:
yaśasvī dhruvasandheḥ tu bharato nāma nāmataḥ |
bharatāt tu mahātejā asito nāma jāyata
verses.translation: "From Dhruvasandhi, an illustrious one named as Bharata is begotten, and Bharata begot a highly effulgent son named as Asita...

verses.devanagari:
यस्यैते प्रतिराजान उदपद्यन्त शात्रवः |
हैहयास्तालजंघाश्च शूराश्च शशबिंदवः
verses.iast:
yasya ete prati rājana udapatyanta śātravaḥ |
haihaya tālajaṅghāḥ ca śūrāḥ ca śaśabindvaḥ
verses.translation: "To which Asita, kings like Haihaya-s, Taalajanghaa-s, and the valiant Shashabindu-s have become adversaries and kings in hostility, he had to wage war with them...

verses.devanagari:
तांस्तु स प्रतियुद्ध्यन् वै युद्धे राजा प्रवासितः |
हिमवन्तमुपागम्य भार्याभ्यां सहितस्तदा
verses.iast:
tān ca sa prati yuddhyan vai yuddhe rājā pravāsitaḥ |
himavantam upāgaṃya bhāryābhyām sahitaḥ tadā
verses.translation: "While counterattacking those kings, Asita is dethroned in war and then he reached Himalayas along with his two wives...

verses.devanagari:
असितोऽल्पबलो राजा कालधर्ममुपेयिवान् |
द्वे चास्य भार्ये गर्भिण्यौ बभूवतुरिति श्रुतम्
एका गर्भविनाशार्थं सपत्न्यै सगरं ददौ |
verses.iast:
asito alpa balo rājā kāla dharmam upeyivān |
dve ca asya bhārye garbhiṇyai babhūvatuḥ iti śruti
ekā garbha vināśa artham sapatnai sagaram dadau |
verses.translation: "Asita was with his meagre forces when he was in Himalayas, and there he drew nigh of his Time. At the time of his demise two of his wives were pregnant, and one of two wives gave toxic food to the co-wife for abortion... thus we heard... [1-70-30-31a]

glosses.meaning: Time's, onus, he drew nigh of - breathed his last
his, two, wives, pregnant, they were

verses.devanagari:
ततः शैलवरे रम्ये बभूवाभिरतो मुनिः
भार्गवश्च्यवनो नाम हिमवंतमुपाश्रितः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ śailavare raṃye babhūva abhirato muniḥ
bhārgava cyavano nāma himavantam upāśritaḥ |
verses.translation: "There was a saint named Cyavana, the heir of Sage Bhrigu, who in fascination with best and beautiful mountains then taking shelter on Himalayas.

glosses.meaning: on mountain, best, beautiful, in fascination
on Himalayas, taking shelter, he was there.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र चैका महाभागा भार्गवं देववर्चसम्
ववन्दे पद्मपत्राक्षी कांक्षन्ती सुतमुत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
tatra ca ekā mahābhāgā bhārgavam deva varcasam
vavande padma patrākśī kāṅkśantī sutam uttamam |
verses.translation: "One of the two wives of Asita, the lotus-petal eyed and highly fortunate one queen came there desirous of a best son, and reverenced the sage who is godly in his glow... [1-70-32b-33a]

verses.devanagari:
तमृषिं साभ्युपागम्य कालिन्दी चाभ्यवादयत्
स तामभ्यवदद्विप्रः पुत्रेप्सुं पुत्रजन्मनि |
verses.iast:
tam ṛṣim sā abhyupagaṃya kālindī ca abhyavādata
sa tām abhyavadat vipraḥ putra īpsum putra janmani |
verses.translation: "Another queen Kaalindi who administer food poison to her co-wife has also come to the sage, and she too reverenced him. That sage spoke to her who received poison from her co-wife regarding the birth of her son.
notes: There are variations in reading these lines. While some say that Kaalindi is one who 'gave' toxic food to her sister, while some others say that Kaalindi is the one who 'received' the poisoned food. Here taking the kālindi ca 'Kaalindi also...' it is said that 'Kaalindi is she who has administered poison...' Since she is also pregnant, coupled with the guilt of poisoning, hence the use of ca , she too came to the sage.

glosses.meaning: to him, that sage, on reaching nigh, reverenced
to her - who firstly arrived, who received poison
in the matter of son's, birth

verses.devanagari:
तव कुक्षौ महाभागे सुपुत्रः सुमहाबलः
महावीर्यो महातेजा अचिरात् संजनिष्यति |
गरेण सहितः श्रीमान् मा शुचः कमलेक्षणे
verses.iast:
tava kukśau mahābhāge su putraḥ su mahābalaḥ
mahāvīryo mahātejā acirāt sañjaniṣyati |
gareṇa sahitaḥ śrīmān mā śucaḥ kamalekśaṇe
verses.translation: " 'Oh, highly fortunate lady, a very good son and a very mighty son is there in your womb. Soon you will give birth to a highly vigorous, highly refulgent son and that illustrious one will take birth with toxicity, but there is no need to worry...' So said Sage Cyavana to the queen of Asita who received the poison.

verses.devanagari:
च्यवनं च नमस्कृत्य राजपुत्री पतिव्रता |
पत्या विरहिता तस्मात् पुत्रं देवी व्यजायत
verses.iast:
cyavanam ca namaskṛtya rājaputrī pativratā |
patyā virahitā tasmāt putram devī vyajāyata
verses.translation: "On reverencing Sage Cyavana that husband devout princess whose husband is no more that lady gave birth to a son...

verses.devanagari:
सपत्न्या तु गरस्तस्यै दत्तो गर्भजिघांसया |
सह तेन गरेणैव संजातः सगरोऽभवत्
verses.iast:
sapatnyā tu garaḥ tasyaiḥ datto garbha jighāṃsayā |
saha tena gareṇa eva sañjātaḥ sagaroi abhavat
verses.translation: "Because he took birth along with the poison administered to his mother by her co-wife, he became Sagara, the emperor..."
notes: Parable: When king Asita passed away his queen and this Sagara's mother wanted to commit self-immolation, but this Sage Cyavana dissuades her from it because she is pregnant, and takes her to his hermitage. When she gave birth to Sagara, Sage Cyavana rears up Sagara and teaches him all of the archery by according āgneya astra Fire-missile etc., kingcraft, and scriptures. On one occasion when Sagara asks for the details about his father, Cyavana had to tell all the legend of Asita and his conflicts with yavana-s, and shaka-s. Sagara becoming furious at Haihaya-s, Taalajanghaa-s, and the valiant Shashabindu-s, wars with them and drives them out of this country. While doing so, Sagara makes yavana-s tonsured, śaka-s or so-called Scythians, as half-tonsured, and pārada-s as shaggy haired ones, thus stripping of their Kshatriya-hood. Taking the nearness of name pārada to Persia, it is said that the kings repulsed by Sagara taken domicile in the Middle East and a āryan or a ā riān is Airan or present day Iran, and age-old are Indo-Iranian links. Further, the word Asia has its own nearness to the name of king Asita.

glosses.meaning: with that, poison, along with, who took birth

verses.devanagari:
सगरस्यासमंजस्तु असमंजादथांशुमान् |
दिलीपोंऽशुमतः पुत्रो दिलीपस्य भगीरथः
verses.iast:
sagarasya asya asamañjaḥ tu asamañjāt atha aṃśumān |
dilīpo aṃśumataḥ putro dilīpasya bhagīrathaḥ
verses.translation: "From Sagara it is Asamanja and from Asamanja it is Amshuman, and from Amshuman it is Diliipa, and the son of Diliipa is Bhageeratha...

glosses.meaning: of Diliipa, is Bhageeratha - is the son.

verses.devanagari:
भगीरथात्ककुत्स्थश्च ककुत्स्थस्य रघुस्तथा |
रघोस्तु पुत्रस्तेजस्वी प्रवृद्धः पुरुषादकः
कल्माषपादो ह्यभवत्तस्माज्जातस्तु शङ्खणः |
verses.iast:
bhagīrathāt kakutsthaḥ ca kakutsthasya raghuḥ tathā |
raghoḥ tu putraḥ tejasvī pravṛddhaḥ puruṣādakaḥ
kalmāṣapādo hi abhavat tasmāt jātaḥ tu śañkhaṇaḥ |
verses.translation: "From Bhageeratha it is Kakutstha, from Kakutstha it is Raghu, and Raghu's son is the great resplendent Pravriddha, who is reduced to a human flesh eater, and he is also known as Kalmashapaada... and from him, that Pravriddha, Shankana is born...
notes: This Pravriddha is really a great king in this lineage, but somewhat arrogant. So, at one time he was subjected to the fury of Vashishta and becomes a man-eating demon. But he too got his mystic powers. When he was trying to issue a counter-curse to Vashishta, by taking water into his hand, his wife Madayanti, being a husband devout wife dissuades him to not to counter all-powerful Vashishta. He on listening to his wife drops that water taken for cursing, onto his own feet. Then his accursed water blemished him via his feet. Hence, he is also termed as Kalmashapaada.

verses.devanagari:
सुदर्शनः शंखणस्य अग्निवर्णः सुदर्शनात्
शीघ्रगस्त्वग्निवर्णस्य शीघ्रगस्य मरुः सुतः |
मरोः प्रशुश्रुकस्त्वासीदंबरीषः प्रशुश्रुकात्
verses.iast:
sudarśanaḥ śaṅkhaṇasya agnivarṇaḥ sudarśanāt
śīghragaḥ tu agnivarṇasya śīghragasya maruḥ sutaḥ |
maroḥ praśuśrukaḥ tu āsīt ambarīṣaḥ praśuśrukāt
verses.translation: " Shankana's son is Sudarshana, and from Sudarshana it is Agnivarsna... And Shiigraga is the son of Agnivarsna, and Shiighraga's son is Maru and from Maru it is Prashushruka, and Ambariisha is the son of Prashushruka...

glosses.meaning: from Prashushruka, Ambariisha, it was - the son.

verses.devanagari:
अंबरीषस्य पुत्रोऽभून्नहुषश्च महीपतिः |
नहुषस्य ययातिस्तु नाभागस्तु ययातिजः
verses.iast:
ambarīṣasya putro abhūt nahuṣaḥ ca mahīpatiḥ |
nahuṣasya yayātiḥ tu nābhāgaḥ tu yayāti jaḥ
verses.translation: "Ambariisha's son was Nahusha, the emperor and Yayaati is the son of Nahusha, but Naabhaaga is born to Yayaati...
notes: These names Nahusha and Yayaati also occur in other Puraana-s, indicating them in earlier eras to Ramayana period.

verses.devanagari:
नाभागस्य बभूवाजः अजाद्दशरथोऽभवत् |
अस्माद्दशरथाज्जातौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.iast:
nābhāgasya bhabhūva aja ajāt daśaratho abhavat |
asmāt daśarathāt jātau bhrātarau rāma lakṣmaṇau
verses.translation: "Aja was Naabhaaga's son and from Aja, this Dasharatha is manifest, and from him, from this Dasharatha, these brothers, Rama and Lakshmana are born...

verses.devanagari:
आदिवंशविशुद्धानां राज्ञां परमधर्मिणाम् |
इक्ष्वाकुकुलजातानां वीराणां सत्यवादिनाम्
रामलक्ष्मणयोरर्थे त्वत्सुते वरये नृप |
सदृशाभ्यां नरश्रेष्ठ सदृशे दातुमर्हसि
verses.iast:
ādi vaṃśa viśuddhānām rājñām parama dharmiṇām |
ikṣvāku kula jātānām vīrāṇām satya vādinām
rāma lakṣmaṇayoḥ arthe tvat sute varaye nṛpa |
sadṛśābhyām naraśreṣṭha sadṛśe dātum ar.hhasi
verses.translation: "Oh, best one among men, Janaka, from the beginning this bloodline of Ikshvaaku-s is spotlessly immaculate, immensely impeccable, indomitable, and irreproachable, and in respect of these kings born in this line of blood, oh, king Janaka, I espouse that it will be meetly of you to offer your seemly daughters to this seemly pair of Rama and Lakshmana..." So said Vashishta to king Janaka.

glosses.meaning: oh, best one among men, oh, Janaka
to seemly [pair of brothers,] seemly daughters of yours
